newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn MP urges Europe fund for truck strike damage.
newsitem.headline: Bonn MP urges Europe fund for truck strike damage.

text.p: A European aid fund should be set up to help companies damaged by the French truckers' strike, a German parliamentarian said on Friday.

If the situation worsens, help should be afforded "above all to the small enterprises whose existence is threatened," Dionys Jobst, head of the lower house transportation committee, told German radio.
Such a fund would be "a European matter, in which France would also have to participate," Jobst said. He gave no specifics.

About 1,000 German trucks have been trapped at an estimated cost of one million marks a day, as striking French truckers sealed the borders. Tens of thousands more from other countries have also been stranded.

The French government said on Friday it planned to sign a decree defining working hours for truckers in a bid to end the crippling blockade now in its twelfth day. Drivers were maintaining their strike in a bid for wage hikes.
Jobst criticised French authorities for not acting sooner to prevent blockades being set up at the most important border crossings.
The strike should have been limited to France's "national territory", he said. He rejected criticisms that Bonn had not done enough to help German drivers trapped by the barricades.
He appealed to the French government and the striking French truckers to "allow the German drivers free passage". They were innocent victims of the strike and were paying a heavy price, he said.
